source_refs.note: Book p. 99: 6.5 Geometric Progression, definition, term labels, r = a_n / a_(n-1) (text before 6.5.1)

blocks.text: Ab tak hum ne arithmetic progression (A.P.) parhi, jahan har dafa aik hi number jora jata tha. Aaj hum aik naye qisam ki sequence se milte hain jahan har dafa aik hi number se multiply (zarb) kiya jata hai. Yeh geometric progression (G.P.) hai, aur roz ki zindagi mein yeh bohat milti hai: bank ka munafa, aabadi ka barhna, ya kisi cheez ka har saal aadha reh jana.

Kitab ki definition: geometric progression ya geometric sequence aisi sequence hai jis mein pehli term ke baad har term pichli term ko aik non-zero constant (aisa number jo badalta nahin aur zero nahin) \(r\) se multiply kar ke milti hai. Is \(r\) ko common ratio (mushtarka nisbat) kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Farq ko aik line mein yaad rakhiye: A.P. mein agli term ke liye \(d\) jorte hain, G.P. mein \(r\) se zarb dete hain. Teen misaalein dekhiye:
\(2, 6, 18, 54, \ldots\): har dafa 3 se zarb (\(r = 3\)); terms bohat tezi se barhti hain.
\(3, -6, 12, -24, \ldots\): har dafa \(-2\) se zarb (\(r = -2\)); sign baari baari badalta hai, plus, minus, plus, minus.
\(16, 8, 4, 2, \ldots\): har dafa \(\frac{1}{2}\) se zarb (\(r = \frac{1}{2}\)); terms chhoti hoti jati hain.
Aik kahani socho: aap ne aik dost ko message bheja, us ne do doston ko, un mein se har aik ne do do ko. Har round mein log double: \(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, \ldots\). Yeh G.P. hai jis mein \(r = 2\).

A.P. ki tarah G.P. ki terms ko bhi \(a_1, a_2, a_3\) waghaira likhte hain, aur \(a_1 \ne 0\). \(n^{\text{th}}\) term \(a_n\) hai aur us se pichli term \(a_{n-1}\). Definition ke mutabiq agli term = pichli term \(\times r\), is liye
\[a_n = r(a_{n-1})\]
Dono taraf \(a_{n-1}\) se divide karein to

blocks.text_alt: r equals a n over a n minus 1

blocks.text: Yani common ratio nikalne ke liye kisi bhi term ko us se pichli term se divide kar dein. Jaise A.P. mein \(d\) nikalne ke liye minus karte the, G.P. mein \(r\) nikalne ke liye divide karte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(a_1 \ne 0\) aur \(r \ne 0\) kyun zaroori hai? Agar in mein se koi bhi zero ho to pehli term ke baad saari terms zero ho jayengi (zero ko kisi bhi number se zarb dein, zero hi rehta hai). Phir \(\frac{a_n}{a_{n-1}}\) mein zero se divide karna parega, jo maths mein mumkin nahin (undefined). Is liye G.P. ki koi term kabhi zero nahin hoti.
Khud sochiye: kya \(0, 0, 0, \ldots\) G.P. hai? Nahin, kyun ke \(a_1 = 0\) hai aur ratio nikal hi nahin sakta.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text:
Kaise pehchaanein ke koi sequence G.P. hai ya nahin? Har term ko us se pichli term se divide karein. Agar saare jawab barabar aayein to G.P. hai, aur wahi jawab \(r\) hai.
\(5, 10, 20, 40\): \(\frac{10}{5} = \frac{20}{10} = \frac{40}{20} = 2\), to G.P. hai, \(r = 2\).
\(1, 2, 4, 7\): ratios \(2, 2, \frac{7}{4}\) hain, sab barabar nahin, is liye G.P. nahin. Shuru mein dhoka deti hai, magar aakhri ratio ne raaz khol diya.
Dhyan dein: hamesha baad wali term upar (numerator) aur pehle wali neeche (denominator): \(\frac{a_2}{a_1}\), ulta nahin.

blocks.caption: Arithmetic progression aur geometric progression ka muqabla

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: kya \(\frac{1}{3}, 1, 3, 9\) G.P. hai? Agar haan to \(r\) kya hai aur agli term kya hogi?
Ratios: \(\frac{1}{1/3} = 3\), \(\frac{3}{1} = 3\), \(\frac{9}{3} = 3\). Sab barabar, to G.P. hai aur \(r = 3\).
Agli term: \(9 \times 3 = 27\).
Ab aap khud kariye: \(5, 10, 20, 40, 80\) mein \(r\) kya hai? (Jawab: 2.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. G.P.: pehli term ke baad har term = pichli term \(\times r\); \(r\) non-zero constant (common ratio) hai.
2. \(a_1 \ne 0\); \(a_n = r(a_{n-1})\).
3. \(r = \frac{a_n}{a_{n-1}}\): kisi bhi term ko pichli term se divide karo.
4. Sequence tabhi G.P. hai jab saare ratios barabar hon.
5. \(r\) negative ho to sign baari baari badalta hai; \(r\) aik se chhota (positive fraction) ho to terms chhoti hoti jati hain.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Ulta divide karna: \(16, 8, 4\) mein \(r = \frac{8}{16} = \frac{1}{2}\) hai, 2 nahin.
2. Sirf pehla ratio dekh kar faisla kar dena: \(1, 2, 4, 7\) shuru mein G.P. lagti hai magar hai nahin. Kam az kam do teen ratios zaroor dekhein.
3. G.P. mein minus kar ke \(r\) nikaalna: farq (difference) A.P. ke liye hai, ratio G.P. ke liye.
4. Yeh samajhna ke G.P. hamesha barhti hai: \(r = \frac{1}{2}\) ho to ghatti hai, aur \(r\) negative ho to upar neeche hoti hai.
